four_steps_2_16_s.failure: second sequential 2.16 s raw Richards solve fails nonlinearly

comparison_to_inherited_budget.interpretation: The independently observed same-horizon discretization difference is thousands of times larger than the inherited F-GC44 head budget. This does not calibrate a replacement budget, but it independently confirms that 1e-5 cm is not representative of the active-irrigation temporal scale in this frozen case.

qualified_claims: A conventional same-horizon one-step versus two-half-step comparison is numerically available for the frozen active-irrigation case.
The endpoint head difference is about 0.0464 cm and is independent of the production temporal-certificate operator and acceptance budget.
The four-quarter sequence cannot provide a finer reference because its second 2.16 s substep fails nonlinearly.
No asymptotic convergence order or exact temporal error can therefore be inferred.
The failure pattern is path dependent: a 2.16 s solve from the original origin converges, but the second sequential 2.16 s solve from the evolved state does not.
nonclaims: 0.0463838 cm is not asserted to be the exact truncation error of either trajectory.
RM23 does not define a new production temporal tolerance.
RM23 does not make smaller timesteps generally preferable.
RM23 does not admit the three-model triangle.
next_required_boundary: Audit the scientific provenance of the inherited F-GC44 1e-5 cm temporal budget. If it has no independent active-irrigation basis, define a separate application-specific temporal acceptance requirement before any production-policy change; do not tune that requirement to make RM23 pass.
